title: Verdant Analytics - escalation postmortem follow-up
summary: Follow-up call to review the May 12th outage that impacted Verdant's inference throughput. Redwood and Verdant reviewed timeline, confirmed root cause as an autoscaler + KV-cache eviction interaction causing CPU fallbacks, discussed immediate mitigations, and agreed on reliability improvements including autoscaler patch, stronger cache pinning heuristics, and additional monitoring/alerting. Action items and next steps assigned.
transcript:
[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we wanted to run through the postmortem and make sure we have aligned next steps.
[00:12] Hannah: Thanks, Ethan. Appreciate you carving time. The spike on Tuesday hit our customer-facing endpoints pretty hard, so want to be sure it won't repeat.
[00:25] Priya: yeah, so quick recap from our side — on May 12th at ~14:37 UTC we saw sustained token-latency increase, throughput drop, some requests fell back to CPU workers which spiked tail latency.
[00:40] Marcus: and from our telemetry it looked like the autoscaler started terminating warm pods while KV cache was still hot, so cold starts had to rehydrate, which added overhead — is that right?
[00:52] Priya: exactly, our autoscaler had an aggressive downscale threshold combined with a GC window; the eviction timing plus a small race in the KV cache invalidate path meant some requests hit a not-warmed path, and because of a config mismatch the fallback path routed to CPU instances rather than lower-quant model variants. that cascade caused the latencies.
[01:20] Tom: wait, fallback to CPU — was that a safety policy or a misconfiguration?
[01:25] Priya: a little of both — safety policy intended to keep availability, but the routing table included a CPU-compatible variant that we didn't expect to be used at that scale. So it protected correctness but not SLO.
[01:38] Sofia: from security perspective we also flagged that audit logs didn't surface the autoscaler decisions quickly; we had to stitch events from kube and our tracing — it'd be great if Redwood could emit a higher-fidelity event for scale decisions.
[01:52] Jordan: noted. we already filed an internal ticket to add scale decision events to the control-plane audit stream.
[02:05] Hannah: what's the short term mitigation we applied?
[02:08] Ethan: immediate fixes were — (1) increased the autoscaler cooldown and disabled aggressive downscale for the last 30m of peak windows, (2) updated routing to prefer GPU-quantized fallback variants instead of CPU, and (3) pinned a subset of model shards so KV cache rehydration isn't needed as often.
[02:30] Marcus: those changes helped, we saw the tail latency drop back in our next peak. but want to make sure there are longer-term fixes.
[02:38] Priya: long term we propose a kernel update to the autoscaler which avoids terminating pods with non-empty KV cache, plus adding a per-tenant cache pinning policy and better reheating heuristics. also a unit that checks fallback routing table to avoid CPU fallbacks unless explicit.
[02:58] Hannah: timeline for those?
[03:02] Priya: autoscaler patch — target next week (May 25th) for rollout to staging, production after validation ~June 2nd. cache pinning heuristics — design doc by May 21, implementation in June. routing policy tweak — config gate, we can ship as a config change in 48 hours if Verdant signs off.
[03:20] Tom: we'll need an ops playbook — clear rollback steps, how to detect early, and who to page. can Redwood add a runbook?
[03:28] Jordan: yes, we'll produce a runbook with thresholds and paging rules. we'll also add dashboards for KV cache miss rates, autoscaler decision latency, and fallback routing counts.
[03:42] Sofia: on compliance — we still need the full audit log export for our SOC2 audit; any ETA on richer logs?
[03:50] Ethan: we can deliver an interim export of the raw control-plane logs by EOD May 19, and the enhanced event stream by May 28.
[04:00] Hannah: great. one other ask — can you run a large-scale soak test with our traffic profile? we want to validate under our real patterns (lots of short chats + bursts).
[04:12] Priya: yes, we can coordinate a replay. Marcus, can you share the traffic traces?
[04:16] Marcus: will do, I'll drop a link to the anonymized traces.
[04:20] Ethan: ok, recap & next steps: we'll send the incident timeline and raw logs, ship the routing config change as soon as you approve, run the autoscaler patch in staging next week, produce runbook and dashboards, and schedule the soak test.
[04:36] Tom: thanks, appreciate the responsiveness. we might ask for a small credit for downtime window — what's the process?
[04:42] Ethan: I'll loop in finance, we have an SLA credit process and I'll follow up via email.
[04:48] Hannah: thanks everyone.
[04:50] [meeting ends]
